seen_animation: a.png: Frames 1-2: a stick figure stands upright left of center, with an octagonal circle head inside a tall U of two arm lines raised overhead and one long wavy line running from under the head to the ground as body and legs. Frames 3-4: the arm U tips backward to the left until it lies horizontal at head height, and the body line leans and bends at the top. Frames 5-6: the figure becomes a bridge. The arm lines slant down to the left toward the ground, the head sits inside them, and the long line rises from the shoulders to a peak and descends to the ground on the right. Frames 7-8: the arms stand nearly vertical on the ground with the head between them, and the leg line lifts off the ground and extends to the right. Frames 9-12: the leg line swings up to vertical and then over toward the left. Frames 13-14: the leg line is horizontal to the left. Frames 15-16: the leg line comes down to the ground on the left of the planted arms, so the figure ends in a bridge facing the other way. The grey scenery (bush, tree, grass) slides left through the shot, as if the camera pans right.
seen_film: d.png: A woman in loose trousers stands with her knees bent and her arms raised (1-2). She arches backward (3-4) and reaches back to the left toward the ground in a deep backbend while her feet stay planted on the right (5-6). Her hands land (6-7). Her feet leave the ground and her legs extend to the right (7-8). Her legs swing up through a handstand (9-11) and over to the left (12-14). She comes down with her feet on the ground on the left of her hands (15-16). It is a back walkover. The camera pans right, so the tree moves left.
named_subject: A stick-figure gymnast (doodle with a circle head between two arm lines and one long leg line) performing a back walkover
evidence: Timing matches the film at every key moment of the e.png/f.png sequence. Standing with arms up is held in e1-3 against f1-3. The backbend starts in e4-8 against f4-8. The bridge with feet planted on the right is e9-12 against f9-12. The hands are planted and the feet leave the ground in e13-16 against f13-16. The leg line is vertical (handstand) in e23-24 against f23-25, horizontal to the left in e31-32 against f31-32, and the feet are on the ground left of the hands in e37-38 against f37-38. The figure is placed where the gymnast is in each frame: horizontally near the center-left of the frame with the hands at about the same x as in the film, and the scenery pans left in step with the film's tree. From e13 to e38 the figure is the c.png construction almost line for line: an octagonal head inside an inverted V of two arm lines whose tips rest on the ground, and a long line leaving the apex of the V. g.png shows one continuous path of heads with no reversals: they drift left and down through 7-10, then shift right in small steps from 13 to 37. Between consecutive frames the change is incremental: e5-8 rotate the arm U by about 20-25 degrees per frame, e9-12 lower it step by step, and e17-38 sweep the leg line with even angular steps.
primary_gap: In e1-4 the body is one straight line from under the head to the ground with no knee bend, while the film (f1-4) shows a crouch with clearly bent knees and a backward lean of the hips. As a result the start of the backbend in e5-8 reads as the arm U pivoting about the head, not as the trunk arching back.
closes_when: In e1-4 the long body line shows a forward kink at knee height that matches the film's crouch, and in e5-9 the top of that line moves left and down together with the head, so the arch forms in the body line as well as in the arms.
protect: Keep the exact c.png construction (octagonal head inside the inverted-V arms, a single long leg line from the V's apex, stroke weight and wobble) and the frame-for-frame timing of the hand plant (e12-13), the vertical handstand (e23-24), the horizontal legs (e31-32) and the feet landing (e37-38). Keep the even angular steps of the leg sweep in e17-38, and keep the scenery pan in step with the film.
identity_gap: The second half matches c.png closely. In the standing frames e1-4 the same parts are rearranged (arms as a U above the head, the long line as the body), which is consistent but loses the knee bend the film shows.
